title: Nasdaq Falls Into Correction as Chip Rout Erases the Midterm Rally; Dow Sheds About 1,800 Points
dek: CNBC put the Nasdaq Composite down about 5.4% and the S&P 500 down 4.3% at the 4 p.m. ET update. The Dow fell about 1,844 points, giving back Wednesday's post-election gain.

body:
## The close: a broad selloff

Stocks closed sharply lower on Thursday as the selling in AI and chip stocks spread across the market. CNBC's 4:00 p.m. ET update put the Nasdaq Composite down 5.4%, the S&P 500 down 4.3% and the Dow down 1,844 points, according to [Stock Titan's close recap](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-november-5-2026). All three indexes were headed for their worst day since April 2025, CNBC said.

The Nasdaq's move meets the usual definition of a correction, a decline of at least 10% from a recent high. [Yahoo Finance's live page](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-thursday-november-5-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-oil-rises-chip-stocks-141439950.html) described the index as closing in correction territory. The Nasdaq also fell below its 200-day moving average for the first time since April, CNBC reported at 3:02 p.m. ET.

## Sectors and top movers

All 11 S&P 500 sectors were lower at 1:57 p.m. ET, with technology falling most (CNBC, via Stock Titan). Chip names took the heaviest losses. Nvidia closed down 9.26% at $181.60, and the Invesco QQQ, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, fell 6.49% (Stock Titan). Stock Titan's real-time data also showed AMD down 17.26% at the official close.

The [Trading Economics US index summary](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/stock-market) put the Dow down 3.4% and the Nasdaq-100 down 6.4%, using CFD prices that differ slightly from the CNBC index figures. Treat the index percentages above as CNBC's; the CFD figures are shown for context only.

Outside tech, the CBOE Volatility Index briefly reached 28.09, its highest level since March 31, and the Russell 2000 entered a correction (CNBC, via Stock Titan). Traders' odds of a December rate increase slipped to 70.1% from 82.7% on Wednesday, according to CME FedWatch data cited by CNBC.

## What the close changes

The midterm rally of Wednesday has been fully reversed. The next test is whether chip stocks stabilize when the market reopens Friday, and whether the Nasdaq holds the 200-day average it just lost.

marketImpact.summary: The Nasdaq correction and chip rout raise pressure on AI-linked valuations. Investors are reassessing data-center spending after the Democratic sweep, while the rate-hike debate is now priced less aggressively.
marketImpact.timeframe: Friday, Nov. 6 open, and the next Fed-odds update

Cloudflare and Airbnb conference calls at 5:00 p.m. ET, which may steer software and AI-cloud sentiment (MarketBeat; Cloudflare release).
CME FedWatch odds for a December rate increase, which fell to 70.1% from 82.7% on Wednesday (CNBC).
